what: Trend — is there a dose-response signal at all?
title: Getting started: a start-to-finish dose-response walkthrough
text: dose_trend_test() runs one-sided log-dose trend test. passes = TRUE means monotonic increasing dose-response relationship detected — response rises dose. really saying: passes FALSE, upward dose-response signal model, fitting mechanistic curves warranted. passes, proceed.

what: Comparison — which model wins, and did the extra parameter earn its keep?
title: Getting started: a start-to-finish dose-response walkthrough
text: relative check. two-parameter Beta-Poisson tested one-parameter Exponential (nested limiting case) via deviance_difference extra degree freedom, alongside AIC/BIC deltas. significant_improvement preferred flag winner. really saying: Beta-Poisson always fits least well extra parameter — significant_improvement asks whether extra flexibility bought statistically real improvement, just curve-fit noise.

title: singlehit 0.1.0
text: Converted legacy CAMRA exponential beta-Poisson workflow side-effect-free R package API. Added grouped-binomial bootstrapping, diagnostics, effective doses, tidy summaries, prediction curves, ggplot2 output. Added optional mirai-backed parallel model refits backend-independent reproducible bootstrap samples. Reported chi-squared, AIC, BIC model preferences separately, legacy chi-squared deviance comparison driving primary result. Added machine-readable fit assessments human-readable conclusions keep absolute model adequacy separate relative model preference. Added experimental consensus_model_decision() vote parser chi-squared, AIC, BIC model selections.
